newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rulers, Congress to form panel to ease ties.
newsitem.headline: Indian rulers, Congress to form panel to ease ties.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Thursday that it will set up a coordination committee this week with the ruling United Front coalition, two months after it helped topple a government led by the same alliance.

"The coordination committee will be set up in one or two days," Congress's newly elected president, Sitaram Kesri, told reporters in the Indian capital after a meeting with Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral.
Congress provoked the fall of former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda in April after Kesri withdrew his party's support for the coalition government.

Kesri accused Deve Gowda of failing to combat communalism, a reference to the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) which the United Front and Congress forced from power last year by joining forces.

Congress agreed later in April to renew its support for the United Front when the alliance chose Gujral as its new leader. The two groups decided to set up a joint committee to help smooth relations, but no one has yet been appointed to the panel.
Asked if Congress and the United Front could jointly fight the next election, Kesri said: "I don't see the next election now."
Congress has 140 lawmakers and the United Front 178 in the 545-member lower house, Lok Sabha. The BJP and its allies control 194 votes.
